newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE CANOLA ENDS DOWN ON COMMERCIAL SELLING, CBOT.
newsitem.headline: WCE CANOLA ENDS DOWN ON COMMERCIAL SELLING, CBOT.

text.p: Winnipeg Commodity Exchange canola futures ended down on commercial selling in sympathy with losses on the CBOT soycomplex, traders said.
"UGG and Cargill sold the November with RBC-DS a net buyer," a trader said. "There's talk of rain this weekend but it's hot and dry in Saskatchewan."
November WCE canola crush profit margin fell to -14.33 Thursday from -8.80 Wednesday. Aug-Sep spread at $1.50. Volume was 3,350 lots, or 67,000 tonnes, with 175 hedges.
August canola fell $6 to close at $355 and November lost $2.90 to settle at $357.90.
November flax slipped $1 to settle at $290. Volume was 125 lots.

October western barley rose $0.50 to close at $129.80 with UGG the best buyer as drought concerns continued. December settled up $0.60 at $131.10 with local and commission selling, traders said. Volume was 1,050 lots.
October feed wheat lost $0.10 to $153.90, December fell $0.20 to $153.80 on commercial selling. About 55 Oct-Dec spread at even money. Volume was 565 lots.
December feed peas fell US$2 to US$171. Volume was 80 lots.
XCan sold 25 December oats lost US$2 to US$118 to LFG, traders said.
(All values in Canadian dollars except oats, feed peas.)
